blindSummary:
Same-sex activity was decriminalised in 2008 by presidential decree on constitutional nondiscrimination grounds. Legal gender recognition exists but requires surgery — a resident-facing barrier. There is no anti-discrimination law covering gender identity, and in March 2023 the top court ruled same-sex marriage is not a constitutional right, signalling judicial conservatism. The capital has a visible, established trans community and hosts regional LGBT organising.

No traveler-facing restrictions exist: no bathroom laws, no border friction, no documented police targeting pattern. Social hostility is moderate — a male-dominated traditional gender culture persists, and trans women face documented employment exclusion — but violent targeting is far below the levels documented in this country's most violence-affected neighbours.
blindOutOfScope: The surgery requirement for legal gender recognition and the marriage ruling are resident-facing.
blindSourceSummaries: International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex activity legal since 2008 (by presidential decree); but same-sex marriage ruled not a constitutional human right by the top court (March 2023); no explicit SOGI discrimination protections (an amendment was blocked by the legislature in 2024); harassment, violence and discrimination not formally recognised as hate crimes; conservative religious actors consistently oppose advances.

Crowd-sourced safety data: homosexuality legal, marriage banned, gender change legal but requires surgery, no nonbinary recognition, no hate-crime protections, no employment/housing discrimination protections, blood donation banned (indefinite deferral), conversion therapy not banned. Only 12% approve of same-sex marriage (a regional public-opinion survey 2023, 18th of 22 countries surveyed).

LGBT-diaspora news outlet (Feb 2018): a supreme-court judge in this country withdrew a draft ruling against same-sex marriage after public outcry - part of the court's long-running marriage litigation.

Foreign broadcaster travel desk (Aug 2018): feature on an indigenous autonomous island territory off this country's coast where community rules are set by women - a flourishing recognised 'third gender' role is celebrated, with practical gender equality and tolerance of gender fluidity - a striking cultural counterpoint to national law.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview for this country (updated March 2026): same-sex conduct legal since 2008 (by presidential decree); legal gender recognition possible; but no marriage or adoption, and the March 2023 top-court ruling that same-sex marriage is not a constitutional human right foreclosed domestic avenues; no SOGI anti-discrimination laws (amendments blocked in 2024); police abuse of trans women reported.
LGBT-diaspora news outlet (Oct 2017): a supreme-court judge in this country ruled against same-sex marriage in a draft opinion - the first of the court's rulings in the marriage cases.
blindLocalsOnly: The surgery-required legal-gender-recognition process is resident-facing; the documented employment exclusion affects residents.
blindTangential: The 2008 decriminalisation removed same-sex-conduct exposure for visitors travelling with partners; the 2023 marriage ruling is a climate signal.
